Per theorem

What the failing lines of each theorem have in common, from the reviews.
aime_1983_p1

Both lines verify standalone, so nothing is missing (CONTEXT). L75's goal is literally the RealLogMul postcondition already in scope, and L322 (log w / log z = 60) follows from the carried facts log w = 24 log x, log z = 2/5 log x, log x != 0 by one division. The in-file failures come from the very large accumulated log/positivity context across about fifteen nested haves, each of which re-asserts earlier facts. Scoping the blocks (or adding `Real.log(z) != 0` and a substitution assert for hgoal) closes them without any new mathematics.

aime_1983_p3

Three of the four lines are `// instance of h₀` asserts that Dafny cannot discharge even standalone, although the analogous polynomial-bodied h₀ in amc12a_2021_p22 instantiates fine; the difference is the Real.sqrt term in h₀'s body, whose MathPrelude contract (`x < 0.0 ==> false`, `y*y == x`) pulls every instantiation into nonlinear reasoning. Line 155 is the calibrated nlinarith step. The fix is to emit h₀ instances in a form Z3 accepts (named predicate/lemma) and to revisit the sqrt contract: `ensures x < 0.0 ==> false` also makes any sqrt of a negative argument a contradiction, which is not Lean's semantics (Real.sqrt of a negative is 0) and is a soundness hazard for exactly the by_contra shape used in h₉.

aime_1984_p1

All eight failing lines are Finset.sum manipulations over Real.sum(range(n), ·) that Lean discharges with named lemmas the translator never cited: Finset.sum_congr (pointwise rewrite by h₂ under the binder, lines 57/113), Finset.sum_add_distrib (88/132), Finset.sum_const (93/137) and the concrete Gauss sums Σ(k+1) = 4851 and Σ2(k+1) = 2450 (98/142). Every subgoal is TRUE, so nothing is mathematically wrong and no context was lost; the front-end simply has no Dafny counterparts for these four sum lemmas, and Z3 cannot unfold a 98-term Real.sum or reason about lambda extensionality on its own. Adding RealSumCongr/RealSumAddDistrib/RealSumConst plus a linear closed-form sum lemma to the library and having the translator cite them from the rw/simp hints would close all eight lines. The two induction-helper and linarith steps of this theorem already verify.

aime_1987_p5

Both lines are divisibility steps under an IntDvd predicate that is not defined in the local library (the extractor unfolds it to a mod-based test). Line 47 verifies standalone and only fails under the whole-procedure resource limit, although the `use y^2` witness survives only as a comment. Line 67 is a missing hint lemma: dvd_add_right (library DvdAddRight, stated in exists-form) is needed to pass from d ∣ 10d+507 to d ∣ 507 and was never cited; the exists-vs-mod mismatch means a cite would also need IntDvdIffEmodEqZero. Emitting witness equations for `use` and the DvdAddRight cite (or a direct `assert 507 % d == 0`) closes both.

aime_1999_p11

All six lines are library-interface gaps, not math gaps: three Mathlib facts exist in the library but were never emitted or are typed wrongly — Finset.mul_sum and Finset.sum_congr only exist for set<int>/int -> real and the sums here are over IccN(1,35): set<nat> (lines 24, 59); Real.injOn_tan exists as RealInjOnTan but the Lean hint spelling `injOn_tan.eq_iff` is not in the citation table (line 267); the reduced-rational lemma RatNumDenOfReducedValue is what `m.num = 175` needs (line 341). Line 150 is a precondition the library added to Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos (cos != 0) that Lean does not have; RealCosPosOfMemIoo would discharge it. Line 65 is the 35-term telescoping sum, where the translator emitted only 4 of the 34 sum_Icc_succ_top peels and on the wrong lambda. Adding nat-typed FinsetMulSum/FinsetSumCongr, a citation alias for injOn_tan, and a full peel chain would close the file's structural steps; the trig content itself (product-to-sum, cos(π − x)) is handled elsewhere in the file.

algebra_9onxpypzleqsum2onxpy

Only two lines fail. Line 39 (the Nesbitt-style nlinarith core) already VERIFIES standalone with the cited le_div_iff instance and sq_nonneg hints, so it is a context/resource issue. Line 100 is a field_simp calc step S = (2(x+y+z)·S)/(2(x+y+z)) that needs the cancellation law Real.div(c·S, c) = S for the library's Real.div with c > 0 (mul_div_cancel_left₀); the calc hint block is empty apart from the tactic comment. Citing that one cancellation lemma closes line 100; line 39 needs only scoping.

algebra_abpbcpcageq3_sumaonsqrtapbgeq3onsqrt2

The proof bounds each a/sqrt(a+b) below by 2*sqrt2*a/(a+b+2) via sqrt(z) <= (z+2)/(2 sqrt 2) and then a rational inequality. Two of the six lines (122, 185) VERIFY standalone and are context/resource failures in a 420-line lemma; line 248 is their identical sibling for (c,a) that Z3 left UNKNOWN. The genuine gaps are all multiplicative steps Z3 will not take on its own: the Real.sqrt_le_left goal rewrite plus field_simp (line 64, where the hint lemma is uncited — and the library's `RealSqrtLeLeft`, keyed to Real.sqrt_le_left, actually states this exact AM-GM goal rather than Mathlib's iff, a mislabeled citation key worth fixing), multiplying inequalities by positive factors (248, 359: mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left), and the cubic polynomial inequality behind h₉₀ (331) after a field_simp fraction combination that is never emitted. Emitting mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left instances and the field_simp normal forms as asserts fixes 64/248/359; 331 probably needs a verified helper lemma.

algebra_absapbon1pabsapbleqsumabsaon1pabsa

A single failing line: the instantiation of the quantified have h₂ (x/(1+x) monotone on x ≥ 0) at (|a+b|, |a|+|b|). Both side conditions are in scope and the translator even emitted the instance assert, yet the standalone subgoal is UNKNOWN — the ∀ body Real.div(x, 1.0 + x) ≤ Real.div(y, 1.0 + y) offers no arithmetic-free trigger, so the forall-statement never fires. Rendering quantified haves as callable lemmas (so `apply h₂` becomes H2(|a+b|, |a|+|b|)) or giving the body a triggerable term fixes it; the rest of the file (82 assertions) verifies.

algebra_amgm_sumasqdivbgeqsuma

Four of the five lines are the same `positivity` step 0 < x²/y from 0 < x, 0 < y, which Z3's nlsat does not find; the library already anticipates this with SqDivPos(a, b) (comment at library_new.dfy:1077), so the translator should emit it for positivity on a square over a positive. Line 131 verifies standalone and is pure context/OOR. Note that the lemma's ensures uses Real.div while all body asserts use native `/`; the final goal only bridges through Real.div's `b != 0 ==> q == a / b` postcondition, which held here but is a fragile seam worth normalising.

algebra_apbon2pownleqapownpbpowon2

The root failure is a translation bug at line 28: `induction'` was hoisted into the R14 helper induction_helper_1(a, b, n), whose contract is only 0 < a, 0 < b, while the ambient fact h₅ (∀ k, (a−b)(a^k−b^k) ≥ 0) is proved later in the main lemma, so `exact h₅ n` has no quantified fact to instantiate. Line 38 is a genuine nonlinear step (multiply the IH by the positive factor (a+b)/2, Lean's gcongr) that Z3 proves TRUE but Dafny does not find in-file. The five remaining lines (45, 54, 61, 64, 66) all VERIFY standalone — two of them are literal restatements of the line-45 assertion — so they are pure context/resource failures inside the {:isolate_assertions} helper. Threading h₅ into the helper's requires and emitting a mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right cite at line 38 would leave only scoping noise.

algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3

Four of the six lines (95, 98, 114, 202) live inside h₄'s `by_contra!` branch c < 1, which is inconsistent because 1 ≤ c is provable from a ≤ b ≤ c, a+b+c = 2, ab+bc+ca = 1; the certificates are vacuous and at 202 the requires even contain 3c^2-4c+1 ≤ 0 while the goal is > 0. Lean closes that branch by contradiction, Dafny needs one `assert false` derived from (a-b)^2 = (2-c)^2-4(c-1)^2 = c(4-3c) ≥ 0 with a ≤ b ≤ c, after which the intermediate haves are irrelevant. The two genuine gaps (250, 292) are nlinarith certificates that use the products mul_nonneg (a)(b-a), (b-a)(c-b), (a)(c-b); Dafny emitted the three SqNonneg cites but at most one guarded MulNonneg, so emitting the missing MulNonneg instances (and the (a-b)^2 = c(4-3c) identity) is the fix. The trimmed subgoals for 98, 250 dropped needed hypotheses and should not be read as sufficiency claims.

algebra_bleqa_apbon2msqrtableqambsqon8b

With x = sqrt a, y = sqrt b the proof is elementary algebra; two lines (115, 136) VERIFY standalone (115's goal is literally a requires; 136 verifies only after trimming — pure context). The remaining three are nonlinear steps hidden in Lean tactics: `rw [h₁₀₁, h₁₀₂]` substituting a = x^2, b = y^2 inside Real.sqrt(a*b) (57, a monomial substitution Z3 does not make), `positivity` for a product of positives (161, MulPos exists in the library but is not cited), and multiplying 4y^2 <= (x+y)^2 by 2(x-y)^2 in the by_cases else-branch plus an empty then-branch (144). Emitting the rw target `a*b == (x*x)*(y*y)`, MulPos cites for positivity, and mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left instances for nlinarith closes all three.

algebra_others_exirrpowirrrat

One line: the `assert false` closing the `intro h₅₁` contradiction needs ¬Irrational 2. Lean supplies it inline with the rational witness ⟨2, by norm_num⟩; Dafny's Irrational is an opaque axiom predicate, so without NotIrrationalNatCast(2) (which exists in the library and makes the subgoal TRUE_FROM_LIBRARY) nothing contradicts the asserted Irrational(2.0). Fix: the translator should emit NotIrrationalNatCast(n) whenever a ¬Irrational goal is discharged by an anonymous-constructor rational witness.

algebra_sum1onsqrt2to1onsqrt10000lt198

Five unrelated gaps. The telescoping induction helper (L29) is a translation bug: the Nat.le induction from 2 was re-indexed to a helper proving P(n+1) for all n >= 0, so Lean's `contradiction` branch for m = 1 becomes a reachable, empty branch that must prove P(2) and cannot. The per-term inequality (L145) is genuine nonlinear division (1/sqrt k < 2/(sqrt k + sqrt(k-1))) that only needs staging into the already-cited DivLtDivIff plus sqrt(k-1) < sqrt k. Two hoisted `assert Real.sqrt(1.0) == 1.0` hints (L179, L213) are translator noise placed before the RealSqrtEqIffSqEq(1.0,1.0) cite (one verifies standalone, one needs the cite). The sum comparison (L235) is missing the library lemma Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty (present as FinsetSumLtSumOfNonempty over set<int>, not emitted) and its nonemptiness side-condition. Fixing the helper's base/precondition and emitting the sum-comparison cite are the two substantive fixes.

amc12_2001_p5

Every failing line traces to the Lean proof being pure kernel computation: `apply Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero; rfl` for the divisibility and `rw [filter equality]; rfl` for the product identity, both on 10000!-sized numbers. Dafny's factorial and Int.pow are computable recursive functions that Z3 tries to unfold (out of resource for the whole lemma), while Int.prod over the set comprehension is an uninterpreted {:axiom} function that no evaluation can reach, so no amount of context trimming helps. The only line that verifies standalone is the set-equality rewrite (29), which is also typed `set x: int` versus the goal's `set x: nat`. Closing this theorem would require library lemmas for the closed form (odd product = (2n)!/(2^n n!)) and for 2^n n! | (2n)!, i.e. replacing `rfl` with mathematics; it is otherwise out of scope for the translator.

amc12a_2003_p25

All 15 lines trace to one carried-but-unusable fact: h₃ (= h₂, the iset equality, which is in the requires) is applied at the points 0, 1, -1, 2, -2 and the translator renders each instance as `true <==> (exists x :: true && Real.sqrt(a*(x*x)+b*x) == c)` without emitting the set-extensionality instance itself. Two things then fail: the instances are never derived from the iset equality (L20-L32, INSTANCE), and every later restatement/obtain of the same existential fails even when it is literally in the requires (L38-L55: the only trigger candidate contains arithmetic, so the `exists`/`:|` are trigger-less, as Dafny's own message says). Mathematically the hypotheses are inconsistent (sqrt = -1 or -2 is impossible), which is why the postcondition (L14) verifies standalone and why Lean finishes with nlinarith on sqrt_nonneg. Fix: emit each instance explicitly (membership 0 <= f(c) via RealSqrtNonneg, then membership in the image set), render existentials without the `true`-wrappers and with a trigger-able body, and skolemise once instead of re-asserting at each nesting level.

amc12a_2008_p4

The single failing line is the theorem itself: a telescoping product over IccN(1, 501) that Lean evaluates by 501 rewrites of Finset.prod_range_succ inside norm_num. Real.prod is uninterpreted in Dafny (only prod({}) == 1 and the FinsetProdIccSuccTopNat peel), so the proof needs an induction helper prod(IccN(1,n), k => (4k+4)/(4k)) == n + 1 instantiated at n = 501; nothing in the emitted body attempts this.

amc12a_2008_p8

Two lines, unrelated causes. Line 17 (y = 1 from y^3 = 1, y > 0) verifies standalone, so it is a context/resource issue inside the by-block. Line 63 is a rendering bug for `apply Eq.symm`: it is emitted as a call EqSymm(x, sqrt 2) whose precondition `a == b` is the goal being proved, so Dafny reports an unprovable precondition; the mathematical content (x = sqrt 2 from x^2 = 2, x > 0 via Real.sqrt_eq_iff_sq_eq) is TRUE and the cited RealSqrtEqIffSqEq(2.0, x) suffices once the circular EqSymm call is removed. Fix: treat `apply Eq.symm` as a no-op goal flip in the translator.

amc12a_2009_p15

All 17 failing lines are in one lemma that Dafny abandons with out-of-resource, so half of them (74, 77, 80, 83, 158, 164, 167, 170) are pure CONTEXT: instances of the quantified haves that verify standalone. The mathematical content of the real gaps is the periodicity of powers of I and the block sums: I^(4q) = 1 (line 22, needs pow_mul or an inductive fact on the recursive Complex.pow), the 4-term block sum (line 36, needs a singleton-sum base case and I^(4m+j) values), and the closed form of the sum to 4m, which Lean proves by `induction m` and Dafny's forall statement cannot (line 49). The contradiction branches (98, 143) and the sum-to-4m+1 lemma (151) need instances of the earlier quantified haves at the *symbolic* witness m plus Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top peels and Complex.ext_iff; the translator carried only the literal instances 0..3. Lines 131 and 137 are existential witnesses (`use n / 4`) the translator drops; the DROPPED anonymous have at 138 is harmless (Z3 arithmetic). Line 86 shows h_grouped_blocks' quantifier has no usable trigger (m occurs only under 4*m+1). Most would be fixed by (a) an induction helper for quantified haves, (b) emitting `exact h x` / `use e` instances as explicit asserts, and (c) two library lemmas: ComplexPowMul (or I^(4q)=1) and a singleton IccN sum.

amc12a_2009_p6

The single line verifies standalone: its goal is the postcondition of the cited RealRpowMul(2.0, m, 2n) read right-to-left, so nothing is missing and the in-file failure is context (the surrounding rpow axioms). The other cite, RealRpowMul(Real.rpow(2.0, m), 2.0, n), has its 0 <= x precondition met by the h₂₁ assert on line 19, so no side condition is at fault either. Scoping the by-block, or asserting the symmetric equality, closes it.

amc12a_2009_p7

The single line is inside the R14 induction helper for h_a_formula: the helper's requires carry only the theorem hypotheses, but the Lean step `have h3 := h_diff m` uses the earlier top-level have h_diff (a(m+1) - a m = 4), which was never threaded into the helper. This is a missing-hypothesis translation bug rather than a prover weakness; adding h_diff (and h_a0, h_x) as requires of induction_helper_2 and passing them at the call site closes it, after which the step is a plain instance of a forall.

amc12a_2010_p10

Both failing lines are `forall n: nat ensures ...` statements standing in for Lean `∀ n` haves whose residual proof is `induction n <;> simp_all <;> linarith`; the bodies contain only finitely many instances (h₀ at 0..3; h₆ at n, 1, 0) and no recursion, so Z3 is asked to prove an inductive statement about an arbitrary n (constant difference for all n; closed form a(n) = p + 4(n-1)). The R14 recursive-helper-lemma rule that fired in amc12a_2017_p7 did not fire here (induction combined with <;> inside a quantified have). Emitting a `decreases n` helper lemma per quantified have with `induction n` closes both lines.

amc12a_2013_p4

The single failing line is the field_simp cancellation (5·2^2012)/(3·2^2012) = 5/3: Z3 must derive 3x != 0 from x != 0, unfold the Real.div wrapper, and cancel a symbolic factor in a quotient — nonlinear real reasoning that nlinarith/field_simp do and Dafny's Z3 does not. Emitting the intermediate facts (3x != 0, Real.div == /, cross-multiplied identity) closes it. Secondary concern: Real.pow(2.0, 2012) is a literal-unrolled recursive function and should be kept opaque.

amc12a_2017_p7

The single failing line is the base case n == 0 of the R14 helper lemma for `induction n` inside inductive_step: its ensures is f(2) == 3, which is exactly h₁ instantiated at 2 (1 < 2 ∧ Even 2 → f 2 = f 1 + 1) plus f 1 = 2. Lean's `simp_all` finds that instance; the Dafny branch is empty and the quantified h₁ is not triggered at 2 (Even and tsub are computable, so this is an instance gap, not an encoding one). Emitting the instance assert in the zero branch closes it.

amc12a_2019_p21

This is a complex-number computation around z = (1+i)/√2 with z⁸ = 1; the DROPPED markers for h₂/h₄ are harmless because the dropped fact is the lemma's own requires. Line 22 is a real translation discrepancy: the goal is the ℤ-indexed Icc/zpow sum while the carried h₄ is the ℕ-indexed IccN/Complex.pow sum, and Lean's `exact h₄` has no Dafny bridge (zpow_natCast + reindexing). Lines 15 and 57 both need z² = i and z⁴ = −1 (hence (√2)² = 2 via the uncited Real.sq_sqrt, plus pow_succ/pow_two); line 57 is TRUE but 8-deep Complex.pow unfolding and the product expansion run out of resource without those intermediate facts. Lines 31 and 51 need the 12-term Icc sum unfolded (Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top, uncited) and exponents reduced mod 8 through z⁸ = 1. Emitting the intermediate asserts z²=i, z⁴=−1, a uniform rendering of the two sums, and a sum-unfolding lemma addresses all five.

amc12a_2021_p14

All 20 failing lines come from three mechanical gaps, not from hard mathematics. (A) `Real.logb` is an uninterpreted library function and the Lean hint `Real.logb` (definitional unfolding) is never mapped to the library lemma `RealLogbDef(b, x)`; lines 35, 55, 107, 111, 214, 217 need exactly that instance (with pow(b,k) > 0, != 1 side conditions for the symbolic-base cases). (B) The Finset lemmas the proof uses (sum_congr, mul_sum, sum_const, sum_Icc_succ_top, card) exist in the library only at set<int>/int -> real while the porter emits IccN (set<nat>) with nat lambdas, so lines 73, 88, 92, 101, 201, 207 have no usable cite; nat-typed variants plus an IccN cardinality lemma close them. (C) `k^2` is rendered as `Int.pow(k, 2)` in the statement and some RHSs but `k * k` in the haves (lines 11, 43), so h6 does not match the postcondition; the identical goal written with k*k at line 274 VERIFIES. The rest is division algebra Z3 does not do (58, 212, 237) and three CONTEXT lines (71, 239, 274) where the goal is literally in scope.

amc12a_2021_p18

Both failing lines are `assert prime(5)` / `assert prime(11)` where Lean uses `decide`. The library's `prime` is a `{:axiom}` predicate with only the negative axiom n < 2 ==> !prime(n), so there is no way for Dafny to establish primality of a literal; the falsifier's TRUE verdict just reflects real primality. A computable `prime` body (or a small-prime lemma the translator calls for `decide` on Nat.Prime k) fixes both lines and unblocks the h1 instances that depend on them.

amc12a_2021_p19

All 14 lines sit inside the single Finset.ext proof of S = {0, π/2}. Seven of them are `norm_num` steps on trig literals whose closing simp lemmas exist in the library but were never cited (RealCosPiDivTwo, RealSinPiDivTwo, RealCosZero, RealSinZero); three are the `injOn_cos.eq_iff` step, which maps directly to RealInjOnCos(a, b) with all preconditions already asserted; two are OOR nonlinear/context lines (70, 115). The two enclosing-block failures (22, 438) are instances of the hypothesis h₀ at x, 0 and π/2 that Z3 does not take, aggravated by the `if (forall …) { FinsetExtReal }` guard emitted on line 17 before the forall blocks, which leaves a negated-quantifier disjunction on every path. Emitting the four trig-literal cites and RealInjOnCos, plus explicit h₀ instances, would close essentially every line.

amc12a_2021_p22

All ten lines carry the procedure-level 'out of resource' for one ~1000-line lemma; six (540, 767, 790, 871, 979, 999) are pure collateral: the goal is literally the RealCosTwoMul/RealCosThreeMul postcondition already in scope and the subgoal VERIFIES. The four real gaps are nonlinear algebra in the uninterpreted term c = cos(π/7): the Vieta derivation a = -(r1+r2+r3) from three root equations and distinctness (212), the quartic expansion 2(2c^2-1)^2-1 = 8c^4-8c^2+1 after substituting the carried double-angle facts (640, 865), and the factorization 8c^4+4c^3-8c^2-3c+1 = (c+1)(8c^3-4c^2-4c+1) with c+1 > 0 (672). Nothing is missing from scope; what closes most of it is (i) splitting the lemma / isolating assertions so the resource limit stops firing on verified lines, and (ii) having the translator emit the substituted polynomial identities that nlinarith/ring_nf compute implicitly. Side note: the RealCosSq cites emitted at nearly every trig line introduce Real.pow(cos x, 2) terms (pow is recursive in MathPrelude) that are never used by these goals and only bloat the context.

amc12b_2003_p17

The lone failure is the postcondition itself, and the standalone subgoal VERIFIES: the cited Real.log_mul / Real.log_pow instances reduce the hypotheses to the linear system p + 3q = 1, 2p + q = 1 in p = log x, q = log y, whose solution gives p + q = 3/5. Nothing is missing; the in-file failure is a context/resource effect (note the odd recursive-call quantifier the extractor kept in requires). Trimming context or isolating the final linarith step closes it.
